title: fix(git.repo.test): plan mode previews a file set that apply mode does not run
description:
## .what
git.repo.test --mode plan (the default) previews a narrower file set than --mode apply actually runs. plan appears to list only the test files the diff touched; apply also runs the tests related to each changed source file. the did-you-know line then promises that apply will execute the previewed set.

evidence (measured 2026-09-23, one branch):
| suite | plan | apply | --thorough |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit | 20 | 123 | 234 |
| integration | 17 | 70 | 125 |
| acceptance | 5 | 132 | 131 |
the acceptance row is a 26x understatement: a caller who trusts the preview budgets for 5 files and waits for 132.

## .why
- the plan/apply contract is that plan is apply minus side effects: same selection, no execution. here the two modes disagree on the selection itself, the one matter plan exists to settle
- a verification gate that cites plan mode to state what breadth a run covered records a number no run produced
- invisible from the inside: every printed number is internally honest

## .shape of the fix
1. plan runs the identical selector apply runs, and prints that set
2. if the expansion is costly, show it in tiers rather than skip it, e.g. matched: 17 changed, 70 related, 125 total
3. clamp, seen red first: a temp repo with a changed source file whose dependent tests are unchanged; assert the plan set equals the apply set
4. repair the did-you-know line
not a fix: to narrow apply to the plan set; the related-test expansion is correct
